title: Most Popular Product Each Month
description:
Find the **product with the highest order count** in each month. If there is a tie, the product with the lower `product_id` wins.

**Table: order_summary** — `order_month` (first day of month), `product_id`, `product_name`, `order_count`

Output columns: `order_month`, `product_id`, `product_name`, `order_count`. Order by `order_month`.
schema_sql: CREATE TABLE order_summary (order_month DATE, product_id INTEGER, product_name VARCHAR, order_count INTEGER); INSERT INTO order_summary VALUES ('2024-01-01',1,'Widget A',10),('2024-01-01',2,'Gadget B',8),('2024-01-01',3,'Doohickey C',5),('2024-02-01',1,'Widget A',7),('2024-02-01',2,'Gadget B',12),('2024-02-01',3,'Doohickey C',9),('2024-03-01',1,'Widget A',6),('2024-03-01',2,'Gadget B',8),('2024-03-01',3,'Doohickey C',11);
solution_sql: WITH ranked AS (SELECT order_month, product_id, product_name, order_count, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY order_month ORDER BY order_count DESC, product_id ASC) AS rn FROM order_summary) SELECT order_month, product_id, product_name, order_count FROM ranked WHERE rn = 1 ORDER BY order_month;

test_cases.description: Jan: Widget A (10), Feb: Gadget B (12), Mar: Doohickey C (11) — one winner per month = 3 rows

hints: Use ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY order_month ORDER BY order_count DESC) to rank products within each month.
Add a secondary sort on product_id ASC to break ties deterministically.
Filter WHERE rn = 1 to keep exactly one winner per month.
explanation: January: Widget A leads with 10 orders. February: Gadget B leads with 12. March: Doohickey C leads with 11. ROW_NUMBER() partitioned by order_month and ordered by order_count DESC assigns rank 1 to the top product each month. Filtering rn = 1 yields exactly 3 rows (one per month).
